issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation omits the final clause 'οπου ην το προτερον' (where he was before) and replaces it with 'nơi Ngài vốn ở trước kia' (the place where He was before), but more importantly, it misses the nuance of the Greek 'αναβαινοντα' (ascending/going up). While 'lên' covers 'up', the Vietnamese phrasing 'thấy... thì thể nào' (see... then what) is a slightly different rhetorical structure than the Greek 'εαν... θεωρητε' (if... you see/consider).
